newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela okays Central bank debt refinancing bill.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela okays Central bank debt refinancing bill.

text.p: Venezuela's Congress approved Wednesday a bill that will allow the government to refinance $3.9 billion of its debts with the Central Bank, legislators said.
The debts derive from the early 1990 when the Central Bank put up collateral for the country's Brady debt restructuring.
Under the bill the government will place a mega-bond with the Central Bank to refinance debts totalling $3.7 billion plus another 113 billion bolivars ($240 million).

The Central Bank will "then issue government paper backed by the bond that will gradually substitute for TEMs in the Central Bank's open market operations," congressman Juan Sosa Maury of the Convergencia party, told Reuters.
TEMs are short-term bonds issued by the central bank.
Maury said the law will also boost the Central Bank's sagging balance sheet.
"The bank was technically bankrupt," he said.
The bill now passes to President Rafael Caldera for signing, Maury added, with paper probably first issued in January.
